Senator Tuberville’s Talladega National Forest Expansion Act (S.1350) claims to promote wellness through trail access—but let’s unpack the details. The bill authorizes federal acquisition of 50,000 acres via “willing sellers,” a process ripe for inflated land deals and bureaucratic bloat. While expanding the Pinhoti Trail sounds noble, Section 3 allocates funds for Forest Service administrative overhead instead of direct trail maintenance.

Alabama’s existing Talladega Division already spans 400K acres with only half federally owned—why not optimize current resources before expanding? Conservation matters, but D.C. habitually uses “preservation” as cover to grow agency budgets.

If this were truly about outdoor access, it’d streamline permitting for private trail development instead of centralizing control.
